_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.

_findings.nft -c cannot run in a build container: netlink: Error: cache initialization failed: Operation not permitted. nft -c applies nothing, but libnftables opens a netlink socket and lists the LIVE ruleset before it will look at a file, and that needs CAP_NET_ADMIN over a real netns. The build had none, so the parser never ran and the step exited 1 at STEP 99/148. Fixed by giving it a netns of its own: unshare --user --map-root-user --net nft -c -f. Proved four ways with a fake unshare on PATH - parses / rejects a mutant at line 60 col 56-60 / unshare absent / unshare REFUSED - because the first draft classified unshare's own refusal as 'nft rejected the ruleset' and would have failed the build a second time on a false diagnosis.

_findings.root looked for every user's lid config: Merging the four rescued branches took the workspace to 588 passed / 1 failed, and the failure was a PRODUCT defect. owner_configs resolved another user's config path through the INVOKING process's XDG_CONFIG_HOME, so the uid scan - which is the path the root driver takes - looked for every user's lid config inside root's own XDG directory, and on any machine where that variable is set the owner's pin would have been ignored silently. It is also why the test passed alone and failed in a full run: a gaming.rs test sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the same process. _findings.errexit does not apply to a `!`-inverted: THE defect class of round 21, and it invalidated three of my own fixes from the same day. bash(1) under `set -e` exempts 'any command in a pipeline but the last, or if the command's return value is being inverted with !'. So `set -e; ! grep -q x <<<x; echo REACHED` prints REACHED. Every `! grep` in these Containerfiles is written as a build-time refusal and 46 of them failed nothing — they are mid-stanza, so their status is discarded and the build only ever stops if some LATER command in the same RUN fails. Found by the p1-063 lid agent in its own stanza; it wrote its refusals as `if ... exit 1` from the start and that is the idiom adopted. Ten of the 46 are not greps and were never in reach of the resolver at all: `apex-mux nonsense-verb`, `apex vm create --graphics spice`, `apex secret --help`, `apex recover reset` as root, `command -v qemu-system-x86_64` — all carrying real security decisions and asserting nothing. Fixed in b1d1c5bf; the gate now reports a fourth number and exits 1 on it.
_findings.706489ec misdiagnosed what broke the bui: 706489ec's message says a bare `! grep -q '_keep'` 'failed on a correct file, and `set -eux` made that a failed image build'. It CANNOT have. `git show 5cb71ea0` puts all three polkit refusals in ONE commit with `<allow_inactive>yes` last, so the `_keep` line was mid-stanza from birth and never ran an exit status anybody read. The five-day breakage was the EFFECTIVE assertions: the nft check and the ApexShellKeybinds grep (neither inverted) and `mouse = true` (last in its stanza). Reasoned, not reproduced, by an agent with the same blind spot. Worth keeping as the lesson: a diagnosis written from a plausible mechanism inherits that mechanism's assumptions.

_ci: CI RAN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM, and this is the record of what that cost and bought. pr-validation.yml triggered ONLY on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and the program is forbidden from opening a PR until final integration - so sixty landed items, twelve landings and ~2000 Rust tests had been verified on exactly one laptop. `gh run list --branch roadmap/v2.2` returned nothing at all. Fixed in four commits, each one exposing the next problem: (1) push + workflow_dispatch triggers added; the first run failed in 18s. (2) The parity check cloned apex-shell's DEFAULT branch, so it compared apex-os roadmap/v2.2 against apex-shell main and reported drift on two touchpad defaults - while the two INTEGRATION branches agreed perfectly at 22 settings. It now clones the matching branch and PRINTS which one it used. THE DRIFT IT EXPOSED IS REAL AND IS KEPT: apex-shell main has drag_lock=true and click_method=clickfinger where apex-os main's generator has false and buttonAreas, so whoever does the final integration must land both sides together or opening the Input page silently changes a user's touchpad behaviour. (3) The path classifier read github.event.pull_request.* and died with exit 128 on a push; it is now event-aware and, when no range can be determined, selects EVERYTHING - this file already records four occasions where a selector picked nothing, the job skipped, and the workflow passed. (4) Six confinement assertions in mcp_sidecar_live.rs had never run anywhere but the L16 because the runner has no bubblewrap; installed rather than skipped, because they are the assertions that the sandbox IS a sandbox.
